items.excerpt: Argues that for a decade designers hid behind the interface, and now that AI can generate the interface itself, the craft that remains is judgment, taste and problem framing rather than pixel-pushing.

Proposes treating the real design-system component as a contract in the middle, with Figma and code as two honest copies of it — a shift the author argues becomes urgent once AI agents generate both sides.
Foundry has released SmartRoto, an AI-powered plugin for Nuke, NukeX, Nuke Studio and Nuke Indie that aims to take the grind out of rotoscoping while keeping artists in control of the workflow.

Lightcraft CEO Eliot Mack argues that viral indie projects like Backrooms and Obsession rewrote filmmaking, and that real-time virtual production and AI-assisted tools are finally catching up to give new creators studio-scale ambition.

3Dflow's 3DF Zephyr 9.0 photogrammetry software can now generate 3D Gaussian Splats from source images or video, alongside point clouds and meshes, extending neural radiance-style capture into a production 3D pipeline.

Walks through why LLM-generated UI in Cursor and Bolt lands in an uncanny valley of functional-but-generic layouts, and offers concrete prompt and design-system fixes to push AI output past the tell-tale defaults.

Introduces Hallmark, a design skill for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex that intercepts the default 'AI slop' look — Inter font, purple gradients, identical cards — and steers agent-built UIs toward distinctive, brand-aware design.

A pointed critique of Meta walking back a scrapped AI creative tool, questioning whether the reversal reflects genuine concern for creators or damage control — a signal of how platform AI decisions ripple into design and creative work.
